title: Traceable In Situ Microwave Power Measurement at the Cryogenic Device Plane in a Dilution Refrigerator
authors: Paolo Panetta, Andrea Celotto, Alessandro Alocco, Bernardo Galvano, Luca Fasolo, Emanuele Palumbo, Luca Callegaro, Luca Oberto, Patrizia Livreri, Emanuele Enrico
abstract: Accurate knowledge of the microwave power delivered to a cryogenic device under test (DUT) is essential for the characterization and operation of superconducting quantum circuits. However, this information is difficult to obtain inside dilution refrigerators because of distributed attenuation, impedance mismatch, switch-path repeatability, and temperature-dependent microwave components. This paper presents an in situ measurement method for RF power at the cryogenic device plane. The method uses a custom variable temperature stage (VTS) as a cryogenic thermal-transfer element. The TVS is alternately heated by a four-wire DC heater and by microwave power dissipated in a 20 dB pass-through attenuator. By fitting the thermal transients and comparing the corresponding steady-state temperatures, the absorbed microwave power is inferred from a directly measured DC electrical power through an AC/DC substitution procedure. The finite reflection and transmission of the attenuator are then accounted for by cryogenic two-port scattering-parameter measurements based on a switch-assisted Short--Open--Load--Reciprocal calibration, so that the result is referred to the DUT reference plane. The system is demonstrated in a dilution refrigerator with powers between -43 and -58 dBm at the DUT input plane. The demonstrated relative standard uncertainty ranges from about 2% at -43.9 dBm to about 40% at -57.6 dBm. The proposed approach combines thermal RF power transfer, cryogenic S-parameter correction, and uncertainty evaluation in a measurement architecture compatible with quantum-device experiments, providing a practical route toward traceable microwave-power calibration at millikelvin stages.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, traceable method for measuring microwave RF power directly at the cryogenic device plane within a dilution refrigerator. It achieves this by correlating measured DC heating power with absorbed RF power via thermal transient analysis of a Variable Temperature Stage (VTS). The technique integrates advanced cryogenic S-parameter calibration to provide reliable power readings essential for quantum circuit characterization.
main_problem: Accurately measuring microwave power delivered to a superconducting quantum circuit (DUT) inside a dilution refrigerator is challenging due to various cryogenic signal path losses and mismatches.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated an in situ measurement method, achieving relative standard uncertainties between 2% and 40% across the tested power range (-43 to -58 dBm).
method: The technique combines AC/DC thermal power transfer measurements using a Variable Temperature Stage (VTS) with cryogenic two-port scattering parameter (S-parameter) calibration.
model_or_system: The experiment is performed in a dilution refrigerator, utilizing a custom VTS weakly coupled to the cold finger. The system's thermal dynamics are modeled by analyzing transient temperature changes when heated alternately by DC current and microwave power dissipated via an attenuator.
key_observables: VTS temperature ($T_{	ext{VTS}}$), measured DC heating power ($	ext{P}_{	ext{DC,H}}$), and RF attenuated power ($	ext{P}_{	ext{RF,A}}$).
important_parameters: The measurement range covers powers from -43 dBm to -58 dBm; key derived parameters include the thermal conductance ($G_0$) and background heat load ($P_0$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the temperature difference across the attenuator is negligible compared to uncertainty, and it relies on accurate SOLR calibration for S-parameters.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the experimental setup involving the VTS weakly linked to the Cold Finger, showing connections for DC heating, RF attenuation, and thermometry.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the difficulty of cryogenic power measurement, details the combined thermal/electrical methodology (using transient fitting and steady-state analysis), presents the necessary S-parameter calibration steps, and concludes with experimental results and uncertainty quantification.
why_interesting: While focused on metrology, this work provides a critical enabling technology for quantum physics experiments by ensuring that the input power to sensitive qubits or superconducting circuits is known with traceable accuracy.

A Variable Temperature Stage (VTS) is weakly thermally linked with the Cold Finger (CF) of a dilution refrigerator with baseplate temperature of ∼80 mK. VTS can be heated both with DC and RF through, respectively, a heater (PH) and a 20 dB attenuator (PA). Its temperature is measured with a resistance thermometry bridge (Th). Both Th and H are driven in DC with a 4-wire configuration. Two nominally equal RF lines are driven by Port 1 and Port 2 and read by receivers R1 and R2 of a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA).
